author: FX.Sniffer
text:
Hey Rex, wakey wakey… OK here’s the explanation just open your eyes wide and clear your mind because this is the best I can do on the M15 as you've requested. See below chart and comments.

At [1] price engulfed [2] a DP then it created the FTR.

I consider it FTR because it failed to return to [3].

Then at [4] a retest of the FTR noting that price still didn’t hit the TG it’s supposed to reach as a result of the engulf & FTR, and once again price has created a clone FTR or RBD at [4], because at [5] it has created a lower low and a consumption of the ignored supply now demand at [6].

After the clone FTR/RBD price has dropped with momentum to [7] engulfing on its way the swing low (minor demand/DBR) at [8]. And at [9] before the strong drop happens, price has spiked the clone FTR/RBD adding sellers, and it can be clearly observed on the M5 chart in the same post as a retest of supply or aka by our earth-2 traders (Wolv&Cap) as a hook into RBD and you know the rest of the story.

Now don’t bother yourself with the terms as it doesn’t matter as long as you can observe and understand the price dynamics and its stages.

Peace.

rexed9999 wrote: 3) If my above point one is correct, is the marked blue box an FTR then? It consumed the demand at [8] and could not make it all the way back to source at [9]?

If you're pointing at my chart then true as explained in my post, but if you're pointing at your chart then technically yes but it didn't go to [9] because of the S/R by the high at [6] and the low at [5]. Yo have to pick FTRs carefully, not every time price fails to return is potential FTR. You have to combine your whole knowledge into it. In technical analysis you have to think of price as a machine that has gears in different sizes, the bigger gear needs power and strength to make one rotation and the smaller gears needs less power and strength, and in order to generate enough momentum to make the bigger gear rotate the smaller gears has to rotate multiple rotations in order for the bigger gear to make one rotation. Cycles in cycles this is how price moves.

rexed9999 wrote: 4) Why do you say [8] is a minor demand? It looks like price moved very strongly from [8] and engulfed supply at [6]? How do you qualify between a minor and major supply demand area i.e. what makes [8] different to [1]?

On this TF the source of the rally is the original demand and anything alese would be minor or DP. however, [8] was a retest of broken minor supply on the left making it a DP but not a major demand. once again don't confuse yourself with my terminology, what matters is for you to understand the price characteristics and what does it react to and how.

author: FX.Sniffer
text:
Got a PM that better be answered in public...

The message was saying that in our early days of traditional S/D trading we used to look for candle engulfing pattern and on RTM here almost nobody uses it but the engulf of the zone is in play. So, I have a question: why don't you use the engulfing candle pattern and why do you treat the zone engulfing as more reliable?

My answer is:

I still look at candle engulf when I look for S/D clusters and I look at other candle patterns as well, but the engulfing of areas is more reliable because "Price Dynamics" is not just a simple candle pattern but "a study of price in motion in regards to the supply & demand order flow", in other words; "the history of price action/reaction and behavior in relation to the supply & demand".

Moreover, the candle engulf on HTF could be an engulf of a significant area on LTF, the areas could be decision points or highs and lows which are areas of significant interest and engulfing them means price wants to travel beyond that area, as well as bears or bulls on the other side are starting to weaken.

What if you’re looking at the line chart and you don’t have any candles?!

Think of candle engulfing as the basics of S/D, and the area engulfing as the advanced S/D.

Hey harshrthakkar,

S/D zones/levels are identified by locating the S/D clusters which in turn are identified by locating the balance of the imbalance / the indecision of the decision / the flag of a pole....so whether its an engulfing pattern or a pinbar or an IB or a piercing line or an evening/morning star or a falling/rising three methods it all has to be followed by a decision, therefore its called a S/D cluster / decision point / origin of move / source of move / RBD / DBR / RBR / DBD.
